title: It Doesn't Matter Where You Start

steps.body: Count the same toys left-to-right, right-to-left, or hopping about — the answer never moves. Order is the counter's choice; the amount is not.
steps.narration: Count the same toys left-to-right, right-to-left, or hopping about — the answer never moves. Order is the counter's choice; the amount is not.

widget.prompt: Count 5 toys from the RIGHT this time — show what the count ends on.

commonCounts.feedback: Counting from the right skips nothing; all five toys still get numbers.
That imagines the new direction re-dealing numbers — but each of the 5 toys still receives exactly one, so the count cannot grow.

widget.missFeedback: Start from either side; give each toy one number and the count ends at 5.
widget.successFeedback: Five again — direction changed, the pairing did not.

predict.prompt: Counting the same 5 toys from the right instead — what changes?
predict.reveal: Order is free; the amount is fixed. Every toy still gets exactly one number.

cml.actionGoal: Pair each object with exactly one number and trust the last number said for kch order irrelevance.
invariants: A count pairs objects with number words one to one, and its last word names the whole group — which is why order, spacing, and arrangement can change without changing the answer for kch order irrelevance.
misconceptions: Skipping or double-counting an object, recounting when nothing changed, or believing a spread-out group holds more.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more object joined the group, what would the last counting word become?

widget.prompt: Counting the same 5 toys from the left or from the right — what happens?

options.label: Both counts end at 5
options.feedback: Correct — the order of counting never changes how many there are; every toy still gets one number.

options.label: Counting from the right gives more
options.feedback: Direction adds nothing; the same five toys are paired with the same five numbers.

options.label: Counting from the right gives fewer
options.feedback: That treats changing direction as losing toys — but the pairing still touches all five, so the count ends where it always did.

options.label: Only left-to-right counting is allowed
options.feedback: Any order works, as long as each toy is counted exactly once.

steps.body: As long as every toy is counted exactly once, the pairing ends at the same last number from any direction.
steps.narration: As long as every toy is counted exactly once, the pairing ends at the same last number from any direction.

steps.body: Use a different representation to test the same idea.

widget.prompt: The same five toys are counted from opposite ends. Which result must both paths reach?

hotspots.label: both reach 4
hotspots.feedback: Five toys counted once cannot total four.

hotspots.label: both reach 5
hotspots.feedback: Direction changes the path, not the total of five.

hotspots.label: both reach 6
hotspots.feedback: Five toys counted once cannot total six.

widget.missFeedback: Look for the choice that follows the counting rule exactly.
widget.successFeedback: Direction changes the path, not the total of five.

widget.prompt: Mina counts her blocks: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. How many blocks does she have?

options.feedback: Correct — the last number said, 7, tells how many blocks there are in all.
The count stops at 7; saying one more number would count a block that is not there.
That stops one number early — every block gets exactly one number, ending at 7.
That runs two past the count; the last number spoken is the answer, and it was 7.

widget.prompt: Start at 4. Hop forward 3 times by 1. Where do you land?

commonLandings.feedback: 6 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 7.
8 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 3 hops from 4 to land on 7.

widget.missFeedback: Start at 4 and count on 3: you land on 7.
widget.successFeedback: 4 and 3 more is 7 — each hop says the next counting number.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — count all 3 hops, one number per hop, to reach 7.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count stops after exactly 3 hops, on 7.
